title: Script prototype disposal
summary: Recover 0x4f4bb0 as State::dispose_prototype: release six arrays in original order and then the 76-byte prototype, preserving modulo size arithmetic, callback timing and captured-owner accounting. Original ECX/EDX ABI is expressed by a test-only fastcall declaration; production code uses a portable member method.
test_description: 112 direct original/source comparisons with null and nonnull blocks, zero and wrapping counts, allocator null/non-null results, callbacks mutating later fields, state.global and owner accounting. Assert all seven ordered callback arguments and whole-fixture equality including untouched prototype/state/global bytes and buffers; install FS and check restoration after every oracle call. Independently assert null/zero releases and unchanged prototype bytes.
known_limits: Allocator callbacks record releases without actually deallocating fixture memory; allocator and OS/CRT internals are outside scope.
32-bit layouts; null prototype or invalid state/global pointers remain invalid as in the original.
Array field names reflect the Lua-style layout and element widths; full VM traversal, reference ownership and script execution are not recovered.
Only zero-new-size semantics of reference script-reallocate are needed; allocation error, panic and nonlocal transfer paths cannot be reached here.
No matching-byte claim; original private ECX/EDX convention differs from the portable member ABI.
